methodology.kernel_quality_all: Geometric mean of pre-generated-mapping kernel times over PR, PR-SpMV, BFS, CC, CC-SV, SSSP, and BC.
methodology.kernel_quality_controlled: Geometric mean over fixed-work PR/PR-SpMV, fixed-source SSSP, and BC.
methodology.end_to_end: Mapping generation + permutation validation + CSR relocation + reuse * kernel time.
methodology.comparison_direction: A Rabbit/GraphBrew ratio above one means GraphBrew is faster.

validated_recommendations.objective: Highest measured all-kernel ordering quality among the documented non-Rabbit compositions
validated_recommendations.scope: Eleven shuffled-label graphs; seven kernels; mapping cost excluded
validated_recommendations.caveat: The full multi-pass Leiden partition is required for the quality win. A one-pass replacement mapped below Rabbit cost but lost 4.2-5.6% in kernel quality. The full composition does not beat Rabbit end-to-end through reuse 100 in the controlled-work matrix.

validated_recommendations.scope: Eleven shuffled-label graphs; fixed-work PR/PR-SpMV, fixed-source SSSP, and BC
validated_recommendations.caveat: Loses the all-kernel aggregate because CC and CC-SV regress.

validated_recommendations.objective: Low-reuse end-to-end time on the rapid qualifying cohort
validated_recommendations.scope: Five-graph rapid cohort; seven kernels; reuse 1
validated_recommendations.caveat: Rabbit kernels are about 5% faster; the gain comes from cheaper mapping and does not generalize to Friendster versus Rabbit Boost.

validated_recommendations.scope: Rule derived on 18 graphs and frozen before 12 untouched holdouts; seven measured kernels
validated_recommendations.caveat: Requires explicit reuse <=2 and Boost Rabbit fallback; the candidate is not a universal static winner.

rejected_or_unvalidated_recommendations.claim: HRAB is generally the best locality choice
rejected_or_unvalidated_recommendations.reason: The best method varies by graph type and kernel; controlled one-axis supergraph ordering was harmful on average.

rejected_or_unvalidated_recommendations.claim: HUBCLUSTERDBG is often within 10% of the best on any graph
rejected_or_unvalidated_recommendations.reason: No bound establishing this statement exists in the frozen matrices.

rejected_or_unvalidated_recommendations.claim: Streaming is preferred for dynamic or memory-constrained graphs
rejected_or_unvalidated_recommendations.reason: The frozen study does not measure dynamic updates, and no complete peak-memory superiority gate supports a performance recommendation.

rejected_or_unvalidated_recommendations.claim: A graph type alone determines the best ordering
rejected_or_unvalidated_recommendations.reason: Kernel choice changes winners within a graph, and most type-specific gains over one fixed Leiden method are small.

rejected_or_unvalidated_recommendations.claim: One-pass Leiden can replace the full partition in the Gorder8 quality winner
rejected_or_unvalidated_recommendations.reason: The one-pass SizeDesc-Gorder8 mapping is cheaper than both Rabbits but Rabbit kernels are 4.2-5.6% faster in the five-graph all-draw confirmation.

rejected_or_unvalidated_recommendations.claim: The promoted cost-matched composition is a universal static winner
rejected_or_unvalidated_recommendations.reason: The eleven-graph gate fails on road/mesh quality and large-graph mapping cost; the validated contribution is the frozen graph-feature and reuse selector.
